Your affinity with chocolate allows you to make a 
homunculus to help you make more chocolate. It is 
friendly to you and your companions, and it obeys your
commands. See this creature's game statistics in the 
Cocoa Homunculus stat block, which uses your proficiency
bonus (PB) in several places.
You determine the homunculus’ appearance, though it is
made entirely out of chocolate. Some chocolatiers prefer to
have the servant adopt a creature-like appearance, while
others make them look like baking equipment, like a sieve or
mixing bowl.
In combat, the homunculus shares your initiative count,
but it takes its turn immediately after yours. It can move and
use its reaction on its own, but the only action it takes on its
turn is the Dodge action, unless you take a bonus action on
your turn to command it to take another action. That action
can be one in its stat block or some other action. If you are
incapacitated, the homunculus can take any action of its
choice, not just Dodge.
A creature of your choice can use an action to eat the
homunculus. When it does, it regains a number of hit points
equal to 1d6 + your wizard level, and the homunculus is
reduced to 0 hit points and dies.
If the homunculus has died within the last hour, you can
use your cook’s utensils as an action to create a new one,
provided you expend a spell slot of 1st level or higher. The
new homunculus appears within 5 feet of you after 1 minute.
At the end of a long rest, you can create a new homunculus
if you have your cook’s utensils with you. If you already have a
homunculus from this feature, the first one immediately
perishes. The homunculus also perishes if you die.

At 10th level, whenever a creature within 20 feet of you casts a spell of a level for which you have spell slots, you can use  your reaction to have your mimic grimoire absorb that spell's essence, temporarily adding it to your list of prepared spells.

It remains on the list for up to 4 hours, and you can only cast it through your grimoire. You may only have one absorbed spell at a time.



Additionally, while it remains in the grimoire, you can choose to permanently exchange one of your spells known for the absorbed spell. If you do, the replaced spell is removed from your list of spells known. This can be done only once per long rest.

Beginning when you select this tradition at 2nd level,
the gold and time you must spend to copy a spell with
the fleshwarping spell tag into your spellbook is halved.

Starting at 2nd level, when you make a Stealth check, you can
add your intelligence modifier to your roll.
You are immune to the frightened condition, and whenever you make a death saving throw you can expend a use of Bardic Inspiration, roll it. and add the result to your roll.

At 6th level, you know the Thunderclap cantrip as well as the Thunderwave and Shatter spells. These do not count towards  your spells known. Additionally, when you reduce a creature to 0 hit points or score a critical hit, you can cast Thunderclap, Thunderwave or Shatter as a bonus action. You must still spend a spell slot as normal.

Your skill with puppetry transcends the physical. You can add your proficiency bonus to ability checks you make that  involve puppets, and you learn the stroke of lunacyOES cantrip. If you already know it, you instead learn one bard cantrip of your choice.

Your dolls gain a limited spark of sentience, though they still rely on your magic to act. Your dolls no longer require your commands to move, take actions other than the Dodge action, combine into a formation, or take reactions; you can still control them in combat (even while incapacitated) as they unerringly follow your mental directions. Additionally, your dolls gain the following traits: Coordinated Assault. The doll has advantage on an attack roll against a creature if another doll is within 5 feet of the creature and that doll isn't incapacitated. Evasion. If the doll is subjected to an effect that allows it to make a Dexterity saving throw to take only half damage, it instead takes no damage on a success, and only half damage on a failure. Return Inanimateness. When the doll dies, you can use your reaction to violently release the magic that animates it and cause an explosion in a 20-foot radius around the doll. Each creature in the area must make a Dexterity saving throw against your spell save DC, taking 8d6 force damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one. The doll is then destroyed, and the maximum number of dolls you can control is reduced by one until you finish a long rest.

You exude an alluring disposition that sways others toward you. If you speak to a humanoid alone for at least 1 minute, you can make a Charisma (Persuasion) check contested by its Wisdom (Insight) check. If you succeed on the check, the target is charmed by you for a number of hours equal to your sorcerer level. While charmed in this way, the target idolizes you and will attempt to follow your demands as best it can, although it will avoid violence unless it was already inclined to fight on your behalf. The effect ends early if it takes any damage, if you attack it, or if it witnesses you attacking or damaging any of its allies. If the target succeeds on the check, the target has no hint that you tried to charm it. Once you succeed on the ability check for this feature, you can't use this feature again until you finish a long rest.

You can transfer your metallic properties onto others. As an action, you can spend 2 sorcery points and touch a willing creature (including yourself), bestowing one benefit from your Steel Skin feature. A creature can only be affected by one benefit from this feature at a time. If you use this feature when a creature is already affected, the old benefit immediately ends and the new one is applied. This benefit lasts until the creature finishes a long rest

You are trained to fight toe-to-toe against martial fighters. 
You gain proficiency in light and medium armour, as well as
the Athletics skill. You can also use armour you’re proficient
in as a spellcasting focus for your wizard spells.
In addition, you add the shield spell to your spellbook if you
haven’t already. You always have this spell prepared and it
doesn’t count against the number of spells you can prepare
each day.

As a.School of Mythos wizard, you know there is a.bigger and older power that you can reach and are willing to pay the price of studying and mastering it.

At 3rd level, when a creature within 30 feet of you that you can see makes an attack roll, ability check or saving throw,you may use your reaction and expend one of your Bardic Inspiration die to let out a high-pitched scream of pure metal power! One hostile creature within 30 feet of you must make a Wisdom saving throw (DC 10 + your Charisma modifier +your Bardic Inspiration die roll) or be frightened.

Additionally, each creature within 15 feet of you who fails their roll take thunder damage equal to your Bardic Inspiration die roll. You may use this ability a number of times equal to your Charisma modifier until you take a long rest.

You add the characterizeOES spell to your spellbook if it is not there already, it counts as a wizard spell for you, and it  gains the spycraft tag. You can cast characterizeoEs without expending a spell slot. When you do so, you can target only yourself and another willing creature. While you and the target are affected by this casting of characterizeoEs, the disguise does not appear magical to divination spells.

Once you cast characterizeoes in this way, you can't do so again until you finish a short or long rest, though you can  still cast it normally using an available spell slot.

The coordination between your dolls improves, allowing them to perform sophisticated maneuvers with each other. As a bonus action, you can issue a special command to any number of your dolls. On their turns, these dolls move up to their speed to a space you designate, then use their actions to combine into a Medium formation that lasts for 1 minute, until there's only one doll in formation, or until you choose to end it (no action required). The formation can occupy another creature's space, and vice versa. If a doll in formation moves on its turn, takes an action or reaction, or is incapacitated, it breaks out of the formation until you command it as a bonus action to move to the formation and rejoin it with its action. When the dolls enter formation, choose one of the following effects: Phalanx. The dolls form a defensive line around a creature within the formation's space, protecting it from harm; this formation moves with the creature. The creature gains half cover, and when it makes an attack against a creature within 5 feet for the first time on its turn, each doll in formation can make an attack against the same creature. Whirlwind. The dolls spin around in place, creating a 5-foot radius whirlwind of weapons around the formation; this area is difficult terrain. When a creature enters the area for the first time on a turn or starts its turn there, each doll within formation can make an attack against that creature. You can move this formation up to the slowest doll's speed as a bonus action. You can command your dolls in this way a number of times equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum of once), regaining all uses when you finish a long rest.

You are exceedingly good at making other people pay
attention to you. When you cast a spell that requires at least
one target to make a saving throw to avoid being charmed by
you, you can expend one use of your Bardic Inspiration and
have the targets of the spell roll with disadvantage. You can
also use this feature on spells which state a creature is
unaffected by the spell's effects because it is immune to being
charmed (such as the suggestion spell).

Your connection with your arcane armament has grown, allowing you to enhance your strikes. Beginning at 9th level, when you hit a target with a magic weapon attack you can channel magical energy through your arcane armament to create one of the following effects: The target takes an extra 2d6 force damage. You can expend a spell slot to increase this damage. The damage increases by 1d6 per level of the spell slot you expend. You gain temporary hit points equal to your artificer level. You can force the target to make a Strength saving throw. On a failed save they are knocked prone. You can use this ability a number of times equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum of once), and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

COVETED RECIPE 

Also from 3rd level, after a creature rolls one of your Bardic Inspiration die they may regain hit points equal to the roll.In addition, at the start of a creature's turn,they may spend your Bardic Inspiration die to reroll any saving throw they failed since the start of their last turn (no action required).

A creature can benefit from this feature a number of times equal to their proficiency bonus per long rest.

At 20th level, as an action you may manifest your illusions into being, the lies you revere becoming real. For 1 minute, you gain the following benefits. � Your auras range increases by 15ft. � Any enemies within your aura who can see you when you active this effect must make a Wisdom Saving throw against your spell save DC or become frightened of you and your allies, as long as they are within your auras, for as long as Impossible Made Real remains active. � You and every ally in your aura gains a +1 bonus to AC � Whenever an ally within your auras hits with a a melee weapon attack you may apply a Divine Smite to the attack as if you struck with it yourself. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a long rest.

Starting at 6th level, when you damage a creature that is below 
half their hit point maximum with a spell, that creature takes 
additional necrotic damage equal to your Intelligence modifier if 
they haven’t already taken damage from this feature this turn.

D
eep within hidden dungeons, wizards of the
School of Forbidden Magic push the boundary
of magic into unknown eldritch depths.
Traditional wizarding schools may shun their
practices, yet wizards of Forbidden Magic delve
deep into the dark arts. Yours is the magic of
heresy; you can sacrifice your own flesh and
blood to fuel your spells, and desecrate the souls of the
deceased to harvest their magic.
Wizards of this school are branded as cultists or apostates.
The powers that you learn come with a steep price, but with
them you become capable of both great and terrible feats.

Starting at 2nd level when you choose this
school, you gain an Arcane Vault, a tiny object
which you can use as an arcane focus.
You can use this Vault to dispel and seal
spells.
As an action touch a creature, object, or
magical effect caused by a spell and make an
Intelligence check, DC 10 + the spell's level.
On a successful check, the spell ends on the
target and is sealed in your Vault.
You have disadvantage on the check if the
spell is to high a level for you to cast.
The Vault can seal one spell at a time and can
be emptied with your Stolen Power feature or
during a short rest where you can turn the
power into a temporary hit die that
disappears if not used by the end of
the short rest.

You gain power from rending the souls you have snared. As an action, you can choose any number of creatures you can see that are charmed by you. Each creature must make a Constitution saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failed save, a creature takes necrotic damage equal to 1d8 + your sorcerer level and has its hit point maximum reduced by the same amount. The target dies if this effect reduces its hit point maximum to 0. On a successful save, it takes half as much damage and doesn't have its hit point maximum reduced. Whether the creature succeeds or fails its saving throw, you regain a number of hit points equal to the total damage dealt and the creature is no longer charmed by you. Once you use this feature, you can't do so again until you finish a long rest, unless you spend 6 sorcery points to use it again.

You have steeped yourself in strange magic and ancient lore.associated with death. Whenever you make an Intelligence check to recall knowledge pertaining to rituals or lore related to death, the undead, or the magic of necromancy, you can add double your proficiency bonus to your roll..

Also, whenever you learn a new Bard spell, you can choose.to learn a necromancy spell of your choice from any spell list..

At 1Oth level, your pentagrams are stronger. When you use  your pentagram feature to create a pentagram while another is still active, the first one doesn't disappear. If you then use this feature to create a third one, the one you created first  disappears.



Additionally, whenever you create a warding pentagram,the creature has advantage on all Dexterity and Constitution saving throws it makes as long as it remains within the pentagram. Whenever you create an imprisoning pentagram the creature is restrained, and cannot teleport, move or be.moved by other means as long as it is contained within the  pentagram.

While most artificers are primarily inventors that take up a life of adventure to further their research or test experiments in the field, those known as forgewrights seek out battle for its own sake. Reveling in the thrill of combat, they combine their innovative spirit with their skill as a warrior to forge the signature weapon of a forgewright, an arcane armament.

Beginning at 18th level, you learn the spell bury*. It is a sorcerer spell for you and it doesn't count against the number of sorcerer spells you know. In addition, you can cast the spell by expending 9 sorcery points. If you do so, you can select any number of creatures of your choice to escape the shackles of gravity and not be affected by the spell (including yourself).

At 6th level, you begin to understand how to bend time and space affecting creatures in different ways.



As an action, you can focus on yourself or a creature within 30 feet of you that you can see, and have it be affected by the same effects of the blink, haste or slow spells for up to 1minute. If the creature isn't willing, it must make a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC or be affected.

You have to use concentration for this feature, but you can concentrate on a spell at the same time. If you are concentrating on both, you make Constitution saving throws to maintain concentration with disadvantage. If you fail the.concentration saving throw, you lose concentration on both effects. You can use this feature once per long rest.

commands,and uses the  Restless Spirit stat block, which uses your Spell Save DC,, and proficiency bonus (PB).
